answer: Every claim must be built inside a Quartz room, a live session where the filer's work stays visible to any worker passing by. When a claim is filed, the Quartz desk reads the signed thread of that session within a day, checking for steady human-paced work across real hours, while a watcher echoes what they saw. No room thread, or a thread of scripted bursts, means rejection and a forfeited 300-coin bond, so 1,000 fakes need 1,000 staffed rooms and 300,000 coins in bonds. One operator opened forty rooms at once, every room typed the same lines at the same minute, and the desk voided all forty.
